items.name: Clipchamp
items.summary: Microsoft's video editor, installed on every new Windows 11 account.
items.effect: You lose the built-in video editor. Videos you already made stay where they are.

items.name: News, Weather and Bing apps
items.summary: News, Weather, Finance, Sports, Travel, Health and Food apps that open as web feeds full of ads and suggestions.
items.effect: The News and Weather apps go. The Weather and News tiles of the Widgets board are separate and stay.

items.name: Bing Search app
items.summary: A background helper that sends what you type in Start to Bing.
items.effect: Typing in Start still finds your apps and files. Web results from Bing no longer appear.

items.name: Get Help and Tips
items.summary: Two apps that open Microsoft support pages and show first-run tips.
items.effect: Nothing you use stops working. Windows Settings still has its own links to help.

items.name: Feedback Hub
items.summary: Sends problem reports and suggestions to Microsoft.
items.effect: You can no longer file feedback from this PC, and Windows Insider builds cannot be reported on.

items.name: Microsoft Solitaire Collection
items.summary: A card-game bundle that shows video ads unless you pay.
items.effect: The games go, along with their saved progress on this PC.

items.name: Windows Maps
items.summary: An offline maps app that few people open.
items.effect: You lose the Maps app and any offline maps downloaded for it.

items.name: Microsoft 365 (Office) hub
items.summary: A launcher and advert for Microsoft 365 and Copilot. It is not Word or Excel.
items.effect: The launcher goes. Word, Excel and the rest keep working and can still be started from Start.

items.name: OneNote for Windows 10
items.summary: The older Store version of OneNote.
items.effect: Notes kept in your Microsoft account stay online and can be opened with another OneNote.

items.name: Mail and Calendar (old)
items.summary: The older Mail and Calendar apps. Microsoft ended support for them in favour of the new Outlook.
items.effect: Mail and Calendar stop working. Make sure you use another mail app first. Your mail itself stays with your mail provider.

items.name: Outlook (new)
items.summary: Microsoft's web-based Outlook, installed for you and set to take over from Mail.
items.effect: You lose this mail app. Classic Outlook that comes with Microsoft 365 is not touched.

items.name: People and Skype
items.summary: Old contact and calling apps that Microsoft no longer develops.
items.effect: Nothing current stops working. Skype itself shut down in 2025.

items.name: Microsoft Teams (personal)
items.summary: The chat app pinned to the taskbar for personal accounts.
items.effect: You lose Teams chat for personal accounts. Teams for work or school, installed from your organisation, is a different app and is not touched.

items.name: Microsoft To Do
items.summary: A task list app that syncs with your Microsoft account.
items.effect: Your tasks stay in your account and can be opened on the web.

items.name: Sticky Notes
items.summary: Notes pinned to the desktop.
items.effect: Notes that only exist on this PC are lost with the app. Sign in to Sticky Notes and let it sync first if you use it.

items.name: Power Automate
items.summary: A workflow tool most people never open.
items.effect: Flows you built in it on this PC stop running.

items.name: 3D Viewer, Paint 3D and Mixed Reality
items.summary: Older 3D and headset apps. Microsoft has retired them.
items.effect: You lose the 3D viewer and headset portal. Regular Paint is a different app and stays.

items.name: Cortana and Microsoft Wallet
items.summary: A retired assistant and a payments app that no longer works.
items.effect: Nothing that works today.

items.name: Groove Music and Movies & TV
items.summary: The older music and video players. Windows 11 uses Media Player.
items.effect: Media Player and your files are not touched. Movies you bought from the Microsoft Store can still be played in the Store app.

items.name: Phone Link
items.summary: Mirrors your phone's calls, texts and photos onto this PC.
items.effect: You lose the connection to your phone. Nothing on the phone changes.

items.name: Dev Home
items.summary: A developer dashboard Microsoft has discontinued.
items.effect: Nothing that works today.

items.name: Quick Assist and Microsoft Family
items.summary: Remote-help and parental-controls apps.
items.effect: You can no longer give or receive remote help with Quick Assist from this PC, and family settings are managed on the web only.

items.name: Xbox app and Game Bar
items.summary: The Xbox app, the Game Bar overlay (Win+G) and its helpers.
items.effect: Win+G, game captures and the Xbox app stop working. Games from the Store and Steam still run. The sign-in components that games need are kept.

items.name: Microsoft PC Manager
items.summary: A cleaner and booster app from Microsoft that stays in the tray and keeps suggesting Bing and Edge as your defaults.
items.effect: You lose its one-click cleanup and its tray icon. TidyWindow does the same jobs without a background app.

items.name: Start feed and Widgets runtime
items.summary: The MSN feed behind Start suggestions and the runtime that Widgets use to run in the background.
items.effect: The Widgets board can stop loading and the feed in Start goes. The Windows web experience pack that Snipping Tool and the emoji panel need is never touched. You can also just turn Widgets off in Quiet.

items.name: Microsoft 365 Companions
items.summary: Small People, Files and Calendar helpers that Microsoft adds to the taskbar and starts with Windows.
items.effect: The taskbar companions go. Microsoft 365 apps such as Word and Teams keep working.

items.name: Whiteboard, Sway, Journal and Power BI
items.summary: Office extras that Microsoft pre-installs or promotes and almost nobody opens.
items.effect: You lose these four apps. Boards, sways and journal pages kept in your Microsoft account stay online.

items.name: Mobile Plans and Operator Messages
items.summary: Apps for buying a mobile data plan and reading messages from a mobile operator. Installed even on PCs with no SIM slot.
items.effect: Nothing changes on a PC without mobile data. On a PC with a SIM, you manage the plan in Settings or with your operator's own app.

items.name: Windows App and Remote Desktop (Store)
items.summary: The Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop client, and the older Store version of Remote Desktop. The Remote Desktop Connection that comes with Windows is a different program.
items.effect: You can no longer connect to a Cloud PC or work desktop with these apps. Remote Desktop Connection (mstsc) keeps working.

items.name: Candy Crush and promoted games
items.summary: Games Windows installs and pins to Start for you after setup or a feature update.
items.effect: The games go, along with their progress on this PC.

items.name: Streaming and social apps
items.summary: Spotify, Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, X and similar apps that come pinned to Start.
items.effect: The pinned app goes. The same service still works in your browser, and you can install the real app again whenever you want.

items.name: Antivirus and shopping trials
items.summary: McAfee, a Dropbox offer and shopping links (Booking.com, eBay, Amazon, Priceline) that new laptops ship with.
items.effect: The trial and offer apps go. If McAfee is your active antivirus, uninstall McAfee itself from Installed apps first so that Windows Security takes over.

items.name: Photo and video trial apps
items.summary: Trial editors and tools that PC makers or Windows pin to Start: CyberLink, PicsArt, Photoshop Express, WinZip, Drawboard and similar.
items.effect: The trial apps go. Files you made with them stay where they are, and you can install the full app again whenever you want.

items.name: Copilot app
items.summary: The Copilot assistant app and the pieces that put it on the taskbar.
items.effect: The Copilot button and app go. Copilot on the web in your browser keeps working.

items.name: Copilot+ AI Hub
items.summary: A Windows 11 app that advertises Copilot+ PC features and AI apps.
items.effect: The promotional hub goes. Nothing you use stops working.

items.name: Edge Game Assist
items.summary: An Edge browser overlay that opens inside games from the Game Bar, with Copilot help.
items.effect: The in-game browser overlay goes. Game Bar and Edge itself are not touched.

items.name: Recall
items.summary: Takes screenshots of what you do so you can search them later. Needs a Copilot+ PC.
items.effect: Recall is switched off as a Windows feature, so it cannot take snapshots or be turned back on from Settings. Snapshots it already took are not deleted by this. You can put it back from the Removed tab.

items.name: HP pre-installed apps
items.summary: HP Support Assistant, myHP, Smart, Jump Starts, Privacy Settings and other HP extras.
items.effect: HP's support and update tools go. Drivers are not part of these apps and stay. HP Smart is the printer app: keep it if you print from this PC.

items.name: Dell pre-installed apps
items.summary: Dell Update, SupportAssist, Digital Delivery, Optimizer and other Dell extras.
items.effect: Dell's update and support tools go. Keep them if you want Dell to deliver BIOS and driver updates for you.

items.name: Lenovo pre-installed apps
items.summary: Lenovo Vantage, Smart Experience, Welcome and other Lenovo extras.
items.effect: Vantage's hardware settings (battery limit, performance mode) and Lenovo's update tool go. Keep them if you use those. Glance, which uses the camera to notice when you look away, goes too.

items.name: ASUS pre-installed apps
items.summary: MyASUS and other ASUS extras.
items.effect: MyASUS settings such as battery care and fan modes go. Keep it if you use them.

items.name: Acer pre-installed apps
items.summary: Acer Care Center, Quick Access and other Acer extras.
items.effect: Acer's care and update tools go.

items.name: MSI pre-installed apps
items.summary: MSI Center and its helpers.
items.effect: MSI Center's fan, performance and RGB controls go. Keep it if you use them.

items.name: Samsung and LG pre-installed apps
items.summary: Samsung Settings, Galaxy apps, LG Smart Share and other extras.
items.effect: The manufacturer's settings and update apps go.

items.name: SmartByte and Killer network apps
items.summary: Rivet Networks' SmartByte and Killer Control Center, which prioritise some traffic and are known for slowing down fast connections.
items.effect: The apps and their settings panels go. Killer Control Center users lose the per-app bandwidth rules. If SmartByte still runs afterwards, remove its driver service under Installed apps.

items.name: Surface Hub app
items.summary: The management app for Surface Hub conference-room devices. It sometimes lingers on other PCs.
items.effect: On a Surface Hub the device can no longer be managed with this app. On any other PC nothing changes.

items.name: Audio enhancer apps
items.summary: Dolby Access, Waves MaxxAudio and Nahimic companions that PC makers add for equalizers and spatial sound.
items.effect: The equalizer and spatial audio controls go. Sound itself keeps working through the normal Windows driver. Keep these if you use those effects.

items.name: OneDrive
items.summary: Cloud storage that is built into Windows and starts with every new account.
items.effect: Files stop syncing with the cloud. Your files are never deleted from this PC, and the app refuses to go while Desktop, Documents or Pictures are backed up to OneDrive.

items.name: Microsoft Edge
items.summary: The browser built into Windows. Removing it is blocked by default in some regions.
items.effect: Edge is removed for every user. It only goes if another browser is installed, and the web components (WebView2) that many apps need are always kept. Windows Update may bring Edge back; TidyWindow tells the updater not to.
